key_insight: Optimized flux pulses enable 12-ns controlled-Z gates with intrinsic errors near 2×10⁻⁵, while revealing operating regimes resilient to dephasing.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps superconducting quantum hardware designers balance gate speed, fidelity, and noise robustness, potentially reducing recalibration overhead.
method: Optimize smooth, single-shot flux pulses for directly coupled, frequency-tunable transmons.
Model intrinsic Hamiltonian errors, energy relaxation, and fast and slow dephasing.
Identify dephasing sweet spots and exploit transmon asymmetry for noise resilience.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 12-ns gates near an 11.6-ns theoretical speed limit and dephasing models calibrated against published experimental measurements.
watch_item: The reported intrinsic error excludes decoherence contributions; hardware performance requires validation under device-specific noise.
paper_title: High-fidelity and robust controlled-Z gates for superconducting transmon qubits. I. Intrinsic errors and decoherence
